issue_context.title: Deprecate sqlite3.version and sqlite3.version_info
issue_context.body:
The `sqlite3.version` and `sqlite3.version_info` attributes have historically created some confusion, as they are sometimes mistaken for the SQLite 3 version number. They used to reflect the _pysqlite_[^1] version number, until the external pysqlite package stopped upstreaming changes to the stdlib sqlite3 module[^2], but today they carry no meaning or practical value[^3].

In order to avoid future frustration, I suggest to deprecate `sqlite3.version` and `sqlite3.version_info` in 3.12, and remove them in 3.14.

See also [discussion on Discourse](https://discuss.python.org/t/want-to-update-sqlite-that-came-with-python/13056/6?u=erlendaasland)

[^1]: The sqlite3 stdlib module was forked off of the external pysqlite module around 2005.
[^2]: Somewhere around 2015, IIRC.
[^3]: `sqlite3.version` is set to the value `'2.6.0'`, and `sqlite3.version_info` is set to the value `(2, 6, 0)`.

@erlend-aasland , In most of the doc's, references to version or version_info are directly through `sqlite3` and not `sqlite3.dbapi2`, I thought it might be good to also emit the warning in __init__.py as well. Do you want me to remove it from `__init__.py`?

We need both, otherwise the deprecation warning wouldn't be emitted on `sqlite3.version`. Importing as e..g. `from sqlite3.dbapi2 import _deprecated_version_info as version_info` doesn't trigger the deprecation warning on attribute access (or at all, it seems).

Simple test script:

```python
import sqlite3, sqlite3.dbapi2, warnings
warnings.simplefilter("always")
sqlite3.version
sqlite3.version_info
sqlite3.dbapi2.version
sqlite3.dbapi2.version_info
```
